 Verona stumble: Cesena celebrate at the Bentegodi with Shpendi. Bianconeri spend the night in fifth place
 Calcio 
 Francesconi strikes early, then the Albanian seals the 2-0 win from the spot in the early round 12 clash. Second consecutive win for Diamanti, who leapfrogs Hellas in the table
 Lorenzo Topello 
 20 november (updated at 22:52) - MILANO 
 English 
 Italiano 
 Deutsch 
 Choose Gazzetta as your preferred source on Google 
 Rather than a season, for Verona it feels like an eternal game of snakes and ladders. One step forward, one (or even two) back. The train called consistency, passing through the Bentegodi, only had a single carriage available between Hellas and Cesena in the early match of round 12 in Serie B. And it was the visitors who boarded in a hurry, claiming their second consecutive victory with a 2-0 win that means not only leapfrogging Verona themselves, but also taking fifth place all alone on 18 points. The Gialloblù, on the other hand, collapsed at home (where they had lost only three months ago, against Ascoli on their debut) and failed their test of maturity: Serie A is seven points away, and the risk is that the gap will widen further after the weekend.
 VIDEO: Diamanti: "Non si gioca più per strada? Ecco cosa dovrebbero fare gli allenatori" 
 so many changes
—   Four changes apiece in the starting line-ups: Verona, compared to the 0-0 draw against Mantova before the break, handed starts to Slotsager, Le Borgne, Sezonienko and Mulattieri (the latter up front in place of Mosquera). Cesena were looking to build on their 1-0 win over Catanzaro and brought in four fresh faces from the start: Ilic and Dalla Vecchia, but above all Caprini and Francesconi. The very two protagonists in the opening ten minutes: in the 5th minute, the former Fiorentina man cut inside and shot centrally, and in the 7th minute Francesconi found the net, emphatically turning in Frabotta's cross from the left. A finish worthy of a seasoned centre-forward, nil-one. The Gialloblù responded on 20 minutes with a low drive from Le Borgne deflected behind for a corner. Verona began stepping on the gas in search of an equaliser, with Sarr firing from outside the box off target, then Sezonienko was blocked just as he was about to pull the trigger. Cesena remained in control and could even have doubled their lead when Pagano saw his effort deflected.
 shpendi strikes again
—   In the second half came the two minutes that defined the sliding doors of the match. In the 59th minute, Bernede received the ball inside the box and struck cleanly, but Siano threw his body in the way to turn it behind for a corner. At the other end came the incident that put the game under lock and key: Fiori got into the box and touched the ball, anticipating Frese's sliding challenge; referee Galipò initially let play continue, but was then called to the monitor. He awarded the penalty to Cesena: from the spot, Shpendi scored his ninth goal of the season, a joy he had not tasted since Halloween night away to Sudtirol. Baroni played the Mosquera card to try and at least reopen the contest, but the most dangerous man for the Veneti late on was Ekuban, who was denied by another standout save from Siano. Cesena even toyed with the idea of a third through a couple of mazy runs from D'Andrea, but could comfortably settle for what they had: a goal in each half was enough, giving Diamanti his third win in the last four matches.
